correctness.rationale: For a primitive Pythagorean pair, the even leg is divisible by 4, hence adjacent vertices differ by at least 2 in \(\nu_2\). On \(N\le4\) this yields the explicit bipartition by \(\nu_2\) in {0,1} versus {2,3}; \(N\ge5\) inherits the checked triangle 240,252,275 from \(\Phi_5\). The bundled certificates give independent sets of size 21 and 144 and disjoint matchings of size 6 and 112 in the fully enumerated 27- and 256-vertex graphs. Independent sets supply lower bounds and disjoint edges impose upper bounds |\(\Phi_N\)|-|M|. The standard-library verifier regenerates every vertex and all 351 or 32640 unordered pairs and checks all certificate predicates.

value.rationale: Xiao explicitly defines the prime-box extremal function but proves only a far-threshold asymptotic decay; its first nontrivial exact cases 21/27 and 144/256 supply concrete calibration. The sharp \(N=5\) onset of triangles identifies a structural boundary of bipartite matching methods, a motivated finite cutoff relevant to exact extremal computations. The result exceeds the generic \(N^{N-1}\) odd-valuation lower bound in both N=3 and N=4 and is not just a decimal restatement or a known Euler brick.
